title: Use the Equilibrium Condition
text: The forces on the forearm must add to zero, so you can find the elbow force once all the other forces are known.

title: Use Torque to Find Bicep Force
text: While the forces on the forearm satisfy the first condition of equilibrium, we must use torque to find the bicep force. The total torque about the elbow sums to zero, so the bicep's torque balances the torques from the arm and the book.

title: Determine Net Torque
text: The bicep torque will be positive, and the arm and book torques will be negative. Each torque is $$\tau=rF$$ (all forces are perpendicular, so we don't need $$\sin\theta$$).

title: Calculate Bicep Force
text: Since $$\tau=rF, $$ divide the bicep torque by the bicep's distance from the elbow to get the bicep force. What is the bicep force (in $$\text{N})$$?

title: Find Elbow Force
text: Now that we know the bicep force as well as the arm and book forces, we can find the elbow force. Remember that we are asking for the magnitude of the force.
